summary: The repository contains critical security vulnerabilities including hardcoded admin credentials and secret keys, which expose the system to unauthorized access and token forgery [s1.f1][s1.f2]. High-severity injection risks exist due to command injection in the /export endpoint, SSRF with disabled TLS verification in /cover, and arbitrary code execution via eval() on user input [s1.f3][s1.f4][s3.f1]. Additionally, stored XSS is possible through unescaped innerHTML usage, and weak MD5 hashing is employed for passwords [s3.f2][s1.f5]. Several functional bugs were also identified, including silent error swallowing, undefined variable references causing ReferenceErrors, and lack of proper error handling [s3.f3][s3.f4].

findings.title: Hardcoded admin password in source
findings.detail: Admin password is a plaintext constant in auth.py, exposing credentials to anyone with repo access.

findings.title: Hardcoded secret key for token generation
findings.detail: SECRET_KEY is a static string in source; anyone who reads the code can forge valid session tokens.

findings.title: Command injection via /export endpoint
findings.detail: User-supplied 'name' is concatenated into a shell command with shell=True, allowing arbitrary command execution.

evidence.quote: subprocess.run("tar czf exports/" + name + ".tgz books.json", shell=True)

findings.title: SSRF and disabled TLS verification on /cover endpoint
findings.detail: requests.get fetches an attacker-controlled URL with verify=False, enabling SSRF and MITM attacks.

findings.title: eval() on user input (arbitrary code execution)
findings.detail: applyFilter passes the filter field value directly to eval(), allowing arbitrary JS execution in the browser.

findings.title: XSS via innerHTML with unescaped book data
findings.detail: Book title/author are concatenated into innerHTML without escaping, enabling stored XSS if data contains HTML.

findings.title: MD5 used for password hashing
findings.detail: MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsuitable for password or token hashing; use bcrypt or SHA-256 with salt.

findings.title: Empty catch swallows load errors
findings.detail: loadBooks catches all errors silently, hiding fetch/parse failures from the user and debugging.

findings.title: applyFilter references undefined 'books'
findings.detail: applyFilter uses a global 'books' that is never defined (loadBooks only passes it to render), so it throws ReferenceError.
